accepted_scope: Constructed an equation-driven common soft overlap and rejected its low-order precision claim through grid tests. Identified background-scattering interpolation error by direct physical-Doppler evaluation and tested a defect-only higher-order-background repair. Old parent/inner histories and feedback remain unchanged.
next_target: Reconstruct the original low-frequency inner domain with the tested defect-only/background-scattering method, retaining DC/BR, memory, the derived infrared exterior and the unchanged higher-frequency exterior. Reuse saved histories and physical Doppler events. Test both baseline and corrections on frequency, timestep and forcing-order controls before recomputing canonical stored-moment-subtracted feedback and its paired gas transfer for both windows. Do not substitute the common-band two-sided outer boundary for the physical lower boundary, discard the bridge, or retune a joining window. Compare tiny residuals against their own numerical uncertainty before assigning physical meaning; keep finite-Planck/recoil and emission remainders explicit.
conclusion: The initial near-perfect overlap agreement shared the inherited low-order interpolation error. Physical-shift source checks confirm it; evolving only the small defect with higher-order known-background scattering reduces the worst grid control from 2.784 to 0.001533 of the original band discrepancy and all 18 new controls pass. The repaired common-band prediction lies close to the outer history, pointing to an inner reconstruction repair rather than tuning a window. Both baseline and corrections behave this way; no new physical signal is claimed.
